import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import sparse
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
rng=np.random.default_rng(2)
c=pd.read_csv('cell_snp.counts.tsv',sep='\\t')
n_cells=3639; n_sites=1445
rows=c.cell.values.astype(np.int32); cols=c.site.values.astype(np.int32); a=c.minor.values.astype(float); t=c.total.values.astype(float)
idx=np.arange(len(c)); rng.shuffle(idx); train=idx[:int(.8*len(idx))]; test=idx[int(.8*len(idx)):]
site_minor=np.bincount(cols[train],weights=a[train],minlength=n_sites); site_total=np.bincount(cols[train],weights=t[train],minlength=n_sites); p=np.clip(site_minor/np.maximum(site_total,1),.02,.98)
vals=(a[train]-t[train]*p[cols[train]])/np.sqrt(t[train]*p[cols[train]]*(1-p[cols[train]])+1e-6); vals=np.clip(vals,-5,5)
X=sparse.csr_matrix((vals,(rows[train],cols[train])), shape=(n_cells,n_sites))
Z=TruncatedSVD(n_components=25, random_state=3).fit_transform(X)

def fit_em(K, seed):
    lab=KMeans(n_clusters=K,n_init=20,random_state=seed).fit_predict(Z[:,:20])
    alpha=0.5
    for it in range(80):
        # M-step
        key=lab[rows[train]]*n_sites+cols[train]
        alt=np.bincount(key,weights=a[train],minlength=K*n_sites).reshape(K,n_sites)
        tot=np.bincount(key,weights=t[train],minlength=K*n_sites).reshape(K,n_sites)
        theta=np.clip((alt+alpha)/(tot+2*alpha),1e-4,1-1e-4)
        prior=(np.bincount(lab,minlength=K)+1)/(n_cells+K)
        # E-step
        ll=np.zeros((n_cells,K))
        for k in range(K):
            per=a[train]*np.log(theta[k,cols[train]])+(t[train]-a[train])*np.log(1-theta[k,cols[train]])
            ll[:,k]=np.bincount(rows[train],weights=per,minlength=n_cells)+np.log(prior[k])
        new=ll.argmax(1)
        if np.array_equal(new,lab): break
        lab=new
    # final params
    key=lab[rows[train]]*n_sites+cols[train]
    alt=np.bincount(key,weights=a[train],minlength=K*n_sites).reshape(K,n_sites)
    tot=np.bincount(key,weights=t[train],minlength=K*n_sites).reshape(K,n_sites)
    theta=np.clip((alt+alpha)/(tot+2*alpha),1e-4,1-1e-4)
    prior=(np.bincount(lab,minlength=K)+1)/(n_cells+K)
    trainll=0
    llcell=np.zeros((n_cells,K))
    testll_assigned=0
    for k in range(K):
        per=a[train]*np.log(theta[k,cols[train]])+(t[train]-a[train])*np.log(1-theta[k,cols[train]])
        llcell[:,k]=np.bincount(rows[train],weights=per,minlength=n_cells)+np.log(prior[k])
        pert=a[test]*np.log(theta[k,cols[test]])+(t[test]-a[test])*np.log(1-theta[k,cols[test]])
        # assigned heldout below
    lab=llcell.argmax(1)
    for k in range(K):
        m=lab[rows[test]]==k
        if m.any():
            testll_assigned += np.sum(a[test][m]*np.log(theta[k,cols[test][m]])+(t[test][m]-a[test][m])*np.log(1-theta[k,cols[test][m]]))
    sizes=np.bincount(lab,minlength=K)
    return testll_assigned, sizes, theta, lab

for K in range(2,9):
    best=None
    for seed in [10,20,30]:
        res=fit_em(K,seed)
        if best is None or res[0]>best[0]: best=res
    testll,sizes,theta,lab=best
    print(K,'heldout_ll_per_read',round(testll/t[test].sum(),5),'sizes',sorted(sizes, reverse=True))
PY"

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool

container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:

    type: data
    format: tabular

```

======

Quick usage
-----------

Once installed, check all arguments by typing ``cellsnp-lite -h``. 
There are two modes of cellsnp-lite:

Mode 1: pileup with given SNPs
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This mode genotypes single cells or bulk sample at a list of given SNPs, which 
could be common SNPs in human population (see `compiled candidate SNPs`_), or
called heterouzygous variants from ``Mode 2b`` on its own.

.. _compiled candidate SNPs: snp_list.html


Mode 1a: droplet-based single cells
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

Use both ``-R`` and ``-b`` to pileup droplet-based dataset (e.g., 10x Genomics) with given SNPs.

Require: a single BAM/SAM/CRAM file, e.g., from CellRanger; a list of cell barcodes,
e.g., ``barcodes.tsv`` file in the CellRanger directory, 
``outs/filtered_gene_bc_matrices/``; 
a VCF file for common SNPs. This mode is recommended comparing to mode 2, if a

List of candidate SNPs
======================

A quality list of candidate SNPs (ususally common SNPs) are important for mode 1. If a list of genotyped SNPs is available, it can be used to pile up.
Alternatively, for human, common SNPs in population that have been idenetified
from consortiums can also be very good candidates, e.g., gnomAD_ and
1000_Genome_Project_. For the latter, we have compiled a list of 7.4 million
common variants (AF>5%) with this bash script_ and stored in this folder_.

In case you want to lift over SNP positions in vcf file from one genome build
to another, see our `LiftOver_vcf`_ wrap function.

# List of common variants

This folder stores processed lists of common variants for using the package [`cellSNP-lite`](https://github.com/single-cell-genetics/cellsnp-lite) (recommended) and [`cellSNP`](https://github.com/single-cell-genetics/cellSNP).

print(\"n\",n)
print(\"tag_names\",tag_names)
print(\"unique CB\",len(cb),cb.most_common(20))

complex inputs from the selected wrapper's live schema and verify the created job

import csv, collections
rows=[]
for line in open('snps.tsv'):
    f=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
    # fields: chrom pos ref alt then 3 fields *4 = 12 -> total 16
    gts=[f[4+i*3] for i in range(4)]
    rows.append(gts)
print('sites',len(rows))
# normalize diploid genotype as set? compare exact GT
def key(g):
    if g=='./.': return None
    return tuple(sorted(g.split('/')))
for i in range(4):
    for j in range(i+1,4):
        diff=same=0; known=0
        for g in rows:
            a=key(g[i]); b=key(g[j])
            if a is not None and b is not None:
                known+=1
                if a==b: same+=1
                else: diff+=1
        print(i,j,'known',known,'same',same,'diff',diff)
# unique genotype vectors among 4 samples
vecs=set()
for k in range(len(rows)):

print('distinct sample genotype vectors',len(vecs))
# cluster samples by full vector equality
samples=list(range(4)); print([sum(1 for _ in [])])
# print sites where not all same

    uniq={key(g) for g in gts if key(g) is not None}

        cnt+=1
        if cnt<=10:
            print(pos,gts,uniq)

# Galaxy UDT Implementation Reference

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

```sh
  metadata.tsv \
  meta.data
```

Use this skill after the scientific tool and parameters have been selected. Build
complex inputs from the selected wrapper's live schema and verify the created job
resolved the intended objects.

  order.
- For reference-source conditionals, confirm the job resolved the intended
  history reference or built-in genome rather than a default branch.

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)
- [Execution failures](#execution-failures)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

These are optional implementation examples, not required steps for every UDT.

Use the validated image below when a UDT needs R, S4, or sparse `Matrix`
support:

```text
quay.io/chiujunhao24/udt:rds-sparse-r4.5.3-matrix1.7.5-r1
```

Stage `scripts/inspect_rds.R` as a typed script input. First produce a bounded
JSON structure report without choosing a metadata member:

```sh
Rscript "$(inputs.script.path)" \
  "$(inputs.input.path)" \
  rds_report.json \
  metadata.tsv
```

analysis, run the script again with that exact member name:

```sh
Rscript "$(inputs.script.path)" \
  "$(inputs.input.path)" \
  rds_report.json \
  metadata.tsv \
  meta.data
```

# User-Defined Tools (Beta)

Starting with Galaxy 25.0, users can create their own tools without requiring administrator privileges to install them. These tools are written in YAML, defined through the Galaxy user interface, and stored in the database.

## Differences from Standard Galaxy Tools

Standard Galaxy tools are written in XML and have broad access to the Galaxy database and filesystem during the command and configuration file templating phase, which uses the Cheetah templating language.

---
name: galaxy-udt-authoring
description: Use when implementing or debugging a fresh Galaxy UDT. Covers GalaxyUserTool representation, input and output binding, command rendering, container discovery and selection, resources, optional runtime probes, and execution failures. Read the bundled implementation reference for concrete templates and failure diagnosis.

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

# Galaxy UDT Implementation Reference

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)
- [Execution failures](#execution-failures)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

import pysam, collections, time
p='pooled.infer.donors.q1.bam'
counts=collections.Counter(); qcounts=collections.Counter(); chrom=collections.Counter(); tags=collections.Counter(); n=0; t=time.time()
with pysam.AlignmentFile(p,'rb') as f:
 for a in f.fetch(until_eof=True):
  n+=1
  if a.has_tag('CB'):
   cb=a.get_tag('CB'); counts[cb]+=1
   if a.has_tag('GX'): tags['GX']+=1
   if a.has_tag('GN'): tags['GN']+=1
   if a.has_tag('UB'): tags['UB']+=1
  else: tags['noCB']+=1
  if a.is_duplicate: qcounts['dup']+=1
  if a.mapping_quality>=30: qcounts['mapq30']+=1
  chrom[a.reference_name]+=1
print('reads',n,'elapsed',round(time.time()-t,1))
print('barcodes',len(counts),'total tagged',sum(counts.values()),'tagstats',tags)
print('depth quantiles', [sorted(counts.values())[int((len(counts)-1)*x)] for x in (0,.01,.05,.1,.25,.5,.75,.9,.95,.99,1)])
print('top',counts.most_common(20))
print('qstats',qcounts)
print('chrom top',chrom.most_common(30))
PY"

import numpy as np
from scipy import sparse
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
z=np.load('cell_site_counts.npz'); a=z['counts']; d=a.sum(2); alt=a[:,:,1]; S,C,_=a.shape
p=alt.sum(1)/np.maximum(d.sum(1),1)
g=(d.sum(1)>=20)&(alt.sum(1)>=5)&(a[:,:,0].sum(1)>=5)
ix=np.where(g)[0]
rows=[]; cols=[]; vals=[]
for j,i in enumerate(ix):
 m=d[i]>0; v=alt[i]/np.maximum(d[i],1)-p[i]; v=v*np.sqrt(np.minimum(d[i],8)/8)
 for c in np.where(m)[0]: rows.append(c); cols.append(j); vals.append(v[c])
X=sparse.csr_matrix((vals,(rows,cols)),shape=(C,len(ix)),dtype=np.float32)
e=TruncatedSVD(20,random_state=7).fit_transform(X)
l=KMeans(2,n_init=20,random_state=7).fit_predict(e)
for x in sorted(set(l)):
 idx=np.where(l==x)[0]; print(x,len(idx),'obs',np.quantile(d[:,idx].sum(0),[0,.1,.5,.9,1]),'embnorm',np.quantile(np.linalg.norm(e[idx],axis=1),[0,.1,.5,.9,1]))
print('means obs label', [d[:,l==x].sum()/sum(l==x) for x in sorted(set(l))])
# print lowest/highest cell ids/obs and labels
ids=[x.strip() for x in open('cell_ids.tsv')]
for i in np.argsort(d.sum(0))[:20]: print('low',ids[i],int(d[:,i].sum()),l[i])

List of candidate SNPs

A quality list of candidate SNPs (ususally common SNPs) are important for

def fit_job(args):
 k,seed=args;t=time.time()

 if seed==0 and k>1:

 prob=model.ID_prob;labels=prob.argmax(axis=1)
 result={'k':k,'seed':seed,'elbo':float(model.ELBO_[-1]),'iterations':len(model.ELBO_),'sizes':np.bincount(labels,minlength=k).tolist(),'confident':np.bincount(labels[prob.max(axis=1)>.95],minlength=k).tolist(),'theta':model.beta_mu.tolist(),'seconds':round(time.time()-t)}
 np.savez_compressed(f'models/k{k}.s{seed}.npz',ID=prob,GT=model.GT_prob,theta=model.beta_mu,theta_sum=model.beta_sum,ELBO=model.ELBO_)
 with open(f'models/k{k}.s{seed}.json','w') as f:json.dump(result,f)
 return result

if __name__=='__main__':
 os.makedirs('models',exist_ok=True)
 ad=sparse.load_npz('AD.npz');dp=sparse.load_npz('DP.npz')
 covered=np.asarray((dp>0).sum(axis=1)).ravel();ref=np.asarray((dp-ad).sum(axis=1)).ravel();alt=np.asarray(ad.sum(axis=1)).ravel()
 keep=(covered>=40)&(np.minimum(ref,alt)>=(ref+alt)*.05)
 ad=ad[keep].tocsc();dp=dp[keep].tocsc()
 sparse.save_npz('model.AD.npz',ad);sparse.save_npz('model.DP.npz',dp);np.save('model.keep.npy',keep)
 print('matrix',dp.shape,'nonzero',dp.nnz,'per cell count quantiles',np.quantile(np.asarray(dp.sum(axis=0)).ravel(),[0,.1,.5,.9,1]),flush=True)
 p=np.asarray(ad.sum(axis=1)).ravel()/np.asarray(dp.sum(axis=1)).ravel()

 af=ad.multiply(inv);mask=dp.copy();mask.data[:]=1
 x=(af-mask.multiply(p[:,None])).multiply(1/np.sqrt(p*(1-p))[:,None]).T.tocsr()
 coverage=np.asarray(mask.sum(axis=0)).ravel()
 x=x.multiply((1/np.sqrt(np.maximum(coverage,1)))[:,None]).tocsr()
 svd=TruncatedSVD(n_components=24,random_state=42);z=svd.fit_transform(x)
 np.save('svd.npy',z);print('SVD',svd.singular_values_,flush=True)
 jobs=[(k,s) for s in range(3) for k in range(1,13) if k>1 or s==0]
 with concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
  for r in pool.map(fit_job,jobs):print(json.dumps(r),flush=True)
